newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit falls back on dollar demand by hedge funds.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit falls back on dollar demand by hedge funds.

text.p: The ringgit fell back against the dollar in late Asian trading on Wednesday after talk of further dollar demand by U.S. hedge funds together with interbank buying capped the ringgit's rise, dealers said.
Dollar selling by local exporters coupled with the dollar's weakness against the yen had earlier blocked the rise in the dollar/ringgit at 2.5150 and pushed it down to a low around 2.5120, they said.
"Players bought back the dollar after the ringgit failed to break 2.5120/30," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "But there's good support around 2.5150."
Strong dollar buying by two U.S. hedge funds at the 2.5100 level pushed the dollar/ringgit to a high of 2.5160 in thin overseas markets on Tuesday.
Dealers said many funds were still short dollar and were looking to cover their positions.
But dealers added that Bank Negara was unlikely to allow the ringgit to depreciate much further given that it was not in line with the general weakness of the dollar.
The U.S. unit on Wednesday fell to its lowest level against the yen since November 1996.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5148/53 a dollar against 2.5145/55 at Kuala Lumpur close on Tuesday.
